ds_context: Steam turbines, a common industrial asset, are subject to various failure modes, including rotor imbalance or bowing, blade cracking or loss, journal bearing failure, seal failure, erosion or corrosion of turbine blades, inadequate lubrication of bearings, rotor rub, and thermal stress damage. These failures can be attributed to improper maintenance or installation, exceeding design limits, lack of proper lubrication, vibration or shock loading, corrosive or erosive environment, fatigue due to cyclic loading, or overheating. The degradation mechanisms include wear and tear due to friction, corrosion due to moisture or chemical exposure, erosion due to particulate matter, fatigue due to cyclic loading, and creep due to high temperatures. Catastrophic failure of the steam turbine can lead to significant downtime and repair costs, as well as collateral damage to other equipment or facilities. Regular inspections and maintenance, non-destructive testing methods, and real-time monitoring of operating conditions and performance can help detect and prevent some failure modes, making preventive maintenance crucial for steam turbines to ensure their reliability and longevity.
